## How to use this

Open this file in RStudio (or Positron) from the `school_active_travel`
project, so `here::here()` finds the data. Run the chunks one at a time
with **Ctrl+Shift+Enter** (or *Run All*). Or render the whole page with
**Render** (Ctrl+Shift+K).

You will mostly only edit **one chunk**, [Your choices](#your-choices).
Every other chunk reads those settings. The [Recipes](#recipes) at the
end are small, separate examples you can copy and change.

::: callout-tip
## Keeping memory down

The outputs are filed by the local authority of the home Output Area
(`data/out/od/la=<code>_<name>/`, and the same for `profiles` and
`routes`). Everything here filters on `la` first, so only that
authority's files are opened. A London borough has 300 or more schools
within reach of each Output Area, so keep `MAX_WALK_MIN` low or pick
particular Output Areas and schools there before drawing routes.
:::

::: callout-important
## What is saved, and what is not

The national run saves the **walking** route of every pair: its line
(`routes`), its height every 50 m (`profiles`) and its distance, climb,
steepness and slope-adjusted times (columns of `od`). For **cycling** it
saves only the two **times** (`bike_min_lts2`, `bike_min_lts4`), from
r5r's travel-time matrix, which gives no line. So every line, profile
and climb in the main map and charts is the walking route, even when the
map is coloured by a cycling time; the cycle route may use other
streets. To see cycle routes, [Cycling routes, worked out on
demand](#cycling-routes) routes the pairs you pick by bike while you
wait (`R/bike_routes.R`).
:::

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(arrow)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(ggplot2)
source(here::here("R", "read_helpers.R"))   # out_dir(), od_open(), route_profile(), route_line()

origins <- read_parquet(out_dir("origins.parquet"))                     # 178,605 Output Areas
schools <- read_parquet(out_dir("schools.parquet")) |> rename(school_la = la)   # 21,834 schools
```

## What is available so far

Authorities appear here as their routing tiles finish. An authority on
the edge of a tile can be in this list before all of it is done:
`pct_done` is the share of its Output Areas whose tile has been
gathered.

```{r available}
gathered <- basename(dirname(Sys.glob(here::here("data", "cache", "tiles", "*", "gathered.csv"))))
available <- origins |>
  group_by(la, lad25nm) |>
  summarise(oas = n(), pct_done = round(100 * mean(tile %in% gathered)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(la %in% sub("^la=", "", list.files(out_dir("od")))) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_done), lad25nm)
available
```

Two small helpers for finding codes:

```{r finders}
# Schools whose name matches a pattern (not case-sensitive)
find_school <- function(pattern) {
  schools |> filter(grepl(pattern, name, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
    select(urn, name, phase, low_age, high_age, independent, school_la, postcode)
}
# The n Output Areas nearest a point. Right-click a place in Google Maps to copy its lat, lon
oa_near <- function(lat, lon, n = 5) {
  origins |>
    mutate(dist_m = round(sqrt(((.data$lon - !!lon) * 111320 * cos(!!lat * pi / 180))^2 + ((.data$lat - !!lat) * 110540)^2))) |>
    slice_min(dist_m, n = n) |>
    select(oa21cd, dist_m, la, lad25nm, oac_subgroup, age_5_9, age_10_14)
}

find_school("Stringer")
oa_near(50.8300, -0.1050)    # near Whitehawk, Brighton
```

## What you can choose from

`od_columns()` lists every column of the `od` table and what it means.
Any column marked *number* can go in `COLOUR_BY` or `PROFILE_ORDER`, or
in a filter of your own. Every distance, height, climb, steepness and
Tobler column describes the **walking** route; the two cycling columns
are times only. Give it an authority,
`od_columns("E06000043_brighton_and_hove")`, and it adds the lowest,
median and highest values there, so you can see sensible thresholds.

```{r od-columns}
od_columns <- function(la = NULL) {
  cols <- tibble::tribble(
    ~column,                 ~kind,    ~units,          ~meaning,
    "oa21cd",                "code",   "",              "Census 2021 Output Area of home (its population-weighted centroid). Use in ORIGINS.",
    "urn",                   "code",   "",              "School's unique reference number (GIAS). Use in SCHOOLS; names are in schools.parquet.",
    "la",                    "code",   "",              "Folder of the home Output Area's local authority (2025), code_name. Use in LA.",
    "straight_m",            "number", "metres",        "Straight-line distance from home to school.",
    "route_m",               "number", "metres",        "Length of the shortest walking route on the street network.",
    "circuity",              "number", "ratio",         "route_m / straight_m: how indirect the walk is (1 = as the crow flies). Meaningless for very short straight lines: 999 where the centroid sits on the school, so filter straight_m > 200 first.",
    "walk_min_r5",           "number", "minutes",       "Walking time at 4.8 km/h on the flat from r5r's travel-time matrix. Sets who is in reach (up to 120). Used by MAX_WALK_MIN.",
    "walk_min_route",        "number", "minutes",       "Walking time at 4.8 km/h along the routed path (r5r detailed itinerary); usually within a minute of walk_min_r5.",
    "tobler_min_to_school",  "number", "minutes",       "Walking time home to school allowing for slope: Tobler's hiking function applied every 50 m, scaled so the flat is 4.8 km/h. Uphill and steep downhill are slower.",
    "tobler_min_to_home",    "number", "minutes",       "The same for the walk back, school to home. Differs from the above where the route climbs one way and descends the other.",
    "bike_min_lts2",         "number", "minutes",       "Cycling time at 12 km/h on quiet streets only (level of traffic stress 2; R5 has the rider walk the bike where no quiet street joins up). Empty if over 60 minutes. A time only: no cycle route, profile or climb is saved; see bike_routes().",
    "bike_min_lts4",         "number", "minutes",       "Cycling time at 12 km/h on any street a bike may use (LTS 4). Empty if over 60 minutes. A time only, like LTS 2. (The Brighton test tile, x08_y01, was searched to 120 minutes, so it has times above 60.)",
    "r5_route_m",            "number", "metres",        "Route length as r5r reports it; a check on route_m.",
    "z_home",                "number", "metres",        "Ground height at home (OS Terrain 50).",
    "z_school",              "number", "metres",        "Ground height at the school.",
    "z_max",                 "number", "metres",        "Highest point on the route.",
    "climb_to_school_m",     "number", "metres",        "Total ascent on the way to school: every uphill 50 m step added up.",
    "climb_to_home_m",       "number", "metres",        "Total ascent on the way home.",
    "max_grad_to_school",    "number", "rise / run",    "Steepest 50 m uphill on the way to school (0.08 = 8%). Negative if the route never climbs (then it is the gentlest descent).",
    "max_grad_to_home",      "number", "rise / run",    "Steepest 50 m uphill on the way home.",
    "steep5_to_school_m",    "number", "metres",        "Length of route steeper than 5% uphill on the way to school.",
    "steep5_to_home_m",      "number", "metres",        "Length steeper than 5% uphill on the way home.",
    "steep8_to_school_m",    "number", "metres",        "Length steeper than 8% uphill on the way to school.",
    "steep8_to_home_m",      "number", "metres",        "Length steeper than 8% uphill on the way home.")
  if (is.null(la)) return(cols)
  x <- od_open() |> filter(la == !!la) |> select(all_of(cols$column[cols$kind == "number"])) |> collect()
  stats <- tibble::tibble(column = names(x),
                          lowest = sapply(x, \(v) signif(min(v, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
                          median = sapply(x, \(v) signif(median(v, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
                          highest = sapply(x, \(v) signif(max(v, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
                          pct_empty = sapply(x, \(v) round(100 * mean(is.na(v)), 1)))
  left_join(cols, stats, by = "column")
}

t <- od_columns("E06000043_brighton_and_hove")
```

The other choices take these values:

| Setting | Takes |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `LA` | one `la` from the *available* table above |
| `ORIGINS` | `NULL` (all Output Areas in `LA`), or a vector of `oa21cd` codes in that authority |
| `PHASE` | `"primary"` (schools teaching ages 7–10), `"secondary"` (ages 12–14), or `"any"`; all-through and middle schools count as both where their ages say so |
| `SCHOOLS` | `NULL`, or a vector of URNs (see `find_school()`) |
| `SCHOOL_NAME` | `NULL`, or a regular expression matched to school names, not case-sensitive, e.g. `"Stringer\|Varndean"` |
| `INCLUDE_INDEPENDENT` | `TRUE` or `FALSE` |
| `MAX_WALK_MIN` | 1 to 120, applied to `walk_min_r5` |
| `NEAREST_ONLY` | `TRUE` keeps only each Output Area's nearest chosen school by walking time |
| `COLOUR_BY`, `PROFILE_ORDER` | any *number* column above, in quotes |
| `MAX_ROUTES`, `N_PROFILES` | how many routes to map and profiles to draw |
| `PROFILE_DIRECTION` | `"to_school"` or `"to_home"` |
| `BIKE_ROUTES` | `TRUE` also routes the profile pairs by bike (quiet streets and any street) and maps them beside the walk; `FALSE` skips it |
| `BASEMAP` | any [leaflet provider](https://leaflet-extras.github.io/leaflet-providers/preview/) name, e.g. `"OpenStreetMap"`, `"Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"`, `"Esri.WorldImagery"` |

## Your choices {#your-choices}

**Edit this chunk**, then run it and everything below it again.

```{r settings}
LA <- "E06000043_brighton_and_hove"   # one authority folder, from the table above (column la)

# Origins: NULL for every Output Area in LA, or a vector of codes
ORIGINS <- NULL                       # e.g. c("E00085094", "E00085100")

# Schools
PHASE <- "secondary"                  # "primary", "secondary" or "any"
SCHOOLS <- NULL                       # NULL, or URNs, e.g. c(136843)
SCHOOL_NAME <- "Stringer"                   # NULL, or part of a name, e.g. "Stringer|Varndean"
INCLUDE_INDEPENDENT <- TRUE

# Which pairs
MAX_WALK_MIN <- 60                    # walking time at 4.8 km/h on the flat (walk_min_r5)
NEAREST_ONLY <- FALSE                 # TRUE: only each Output Area's nearest school (by walking time) among those chosen

# Drawing
COLOUR_BY <- "tobler_min_to_school"      # any numeric od column, e.g. "tobler_min_to_school", "bike_min_lts2", "circuity", "climb_to_school_m" 
MAX_ROUTES <- 3000                    # map at most this many routes (the shortest walks first)
N_PROFILES <- 6                       # height profiles to draw
PROFILE_ORDER <- "climb_to_school_m"  # profiles of the pairs with the most of this
PROFILE_DIRECTION <- "to_school"      # "to_school" or "to_home"
BASEMAP <- "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"            # or "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", "Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap"
BIKE_ROUTES <- TRUE                   # also route the profile pairs by bike (loads the tile's street network: about a minute and a few GB)
```

## The pairs you chose

This reads the authority's `od` file, joins the school details and
applies your choices. `sel` is an ordinary data frame: one row per
Output Area and school.

```{r select}
stopifnot("LA is not among the authorities done so far" = LA %in% available$la)
od <- od_open() |> filter(la == !!LA) |> collect()

sel <- od |>
  inner_join(schools |> select(urn, name, phase, serves_primary, serves_secondary, independent,
                               selective, faith, pupils, s_lon = lon, s_lat = lat), by = "urn") |>
  left_join(origins |> select(oa21cd, o_lon = lon, o_lat = lat, oac_subgroup, age_5_9, age_10_14), by = "oa21cd")

if (!is.null(ORIGINS))     sel <- filter(sel, oa21cd %in% ORIGINS)
if (PHASE == "primary")    sel <- filter(sel, serves_primary)
if (PHASE == "secondary")  sel <- filter(sel, serves_secondary)
if (!INCLUDE_INDEPENDENT)  sel <- filter(sel, !independent)
if (!is.null(SCHOOLS))     sel <- filter(sel, urn %in% SCHOOLS)
if (!is.null(SCHOOL_NAME)) sel <- filter(sel, grepl(SCHOOL_NAME, name, ignore.case = TRUE))
sel <- filter(sel, walk_min_r5 <= MAX_WALK_MIN)
if (NEAREST_ONLY) sel <- sel |> group_by(oa21cd) |> slice_min(walk_min_r5, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()
sel <- sel |> arrange(walk_min_r5) |> mutate(label = paste0(oa21cd, " to ", name))

cat(format(nrow(sel), big.mark = ","), "pairs:", n_distinct(sel$oa21cd), "Output Areas,", n_distinct(sel$urn), "schools\n")
```

By school:

```{r by-school}
sel |>
  group_by(urn, name) |>
  summarise(output_areas = n(), median_walk_min = median(walk_min_r5), median_route_km = round(median(route_m) / 1000, 2),
            median_climb_to_school_m = round(median(climb_to_school_m)), median_climb_to_home_m = round(median(climb_to_home_m)),
            pct_with_quiet_bike_route = round(100 * mean(!is.na(bike_min_lts2))), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(output_areas))
```

Every pair, with the columns you are most likely to want (all the `od`
columns are in `sel`; `od_columns()` above says what each one means):

```{r pairs-table}
sel |> select(oa21cd, name, walk_min_r5, tobler_min_to_school, tobler_min_to_home, route_m, straight_m, circuity,
              climb_to_school_m, climb_to_home_m, max_grad_to_school, steep8_to_school_m, bike_min_lts2, bike_min_lts4)
```

## Map of the routes

The lines are the **walking** routes, read only for the pairs in `sel`,
up to `MAX_ROUTES` of them. Coloured by a cycling time, they still show
the walk: the cycle routes are in [their own section](#cycling-routes).
Click a route for its details. The layer control (top right) turns the
routes, Output Areas and schools on and off.

```{r read-routes}
# Route lines for a set of pairs (needs columns oa21cd, urn) in one authority
read_routes <- function(pairs, la) {
  x <- open_dataset(out_dir("routes")) |>
    filter(la == !!la, oa21cd %in% !!unique(pairs$oa21cd), urn %in% !!unique(pairs$urn)) |>   # only these Output Areas and schools
    collect() |>
    semi_join(pairs, by = c("oa21cd", "urn"))
  st_sf(x |> select(oa21cd, urn), geometry = st_as_sfc(structure(lapply(x$geom_wkb, as.raw), class = "WKB"), crs = 27700))
}

to_map <- head(sel, MAX_ROUTES)
rt <- read_routes(to_map, LA) |> left_join(to_map, by = c("oa21cd", "urn")) |> st_transform(4326)
```

```{r map}
#| fig-height: 7
stopifnot(is.numeric(rt[[COLOUR_BY]]))
v <- rt[[COLOUR_BY]]
cap <- quantile(v, 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)                  # so a few extreme routes don't wash out the colours
pal <- colorNumeric(viridisLite::magma(256, direction = -1, end = 0.92), domain = c(min(v, na.rm = TRUE), cap), na.color = "#bbbbbb")
pop <- with(rt, sprintf(
  "<b>%s</b> to <b>%s</b><br>walk %d min (r5r), route %.2f km<br>Tobler: %.0f min there, %.0f min back<br>climb: %.0f m there, %.0f m back<br>steepest: %.0f%% there<br>bike: %s min quiet streets, %s min any street",
  oa21cd, name, walk_min_r5, route_m / 1000, tobler_min_to_school, tobler_min_to_home, climb_to_school_m, climb_to_home_m,
  100 * max_grad_to_school, ifelse(is.na(bike_min_lts2), "none within 60", bike_min_lts2), ifelse(is.na(bike_min_lts4), "none within 60", bike_min_lts4)))
oas <- distinct(st_drop_geometry(rt), oa21cd, o_lon, o_lat)
sch <- distinct(st_drop_geometry(rt), urn, name, s_lon, s_lat)

leaflet(rt) |>
  addProviderTiles(BASEMAP) |>
  addPolylines(color = ~pal(pmin(v, cap)), weight = 2, opacity = 0.6, popup = pop, group = "Routes",
               highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 5, opacity = 1, bringToFront = TRUE)) |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = oas, lng = ~o_lon, lat = ~o_lat, radius = 2, color = "#333333", weight = 1, fillOpacity = 0.6,
                   label = ~oa21cd, group = "Output Areas") |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = sch, lng = ~s_lon, lat = ~s_lat, radius = 6, color = "#222222", fillColor = "white", weight = 2,
                   fillOpacity = 1, label = ~name, group = "Schools") |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = c(min(v, na.rm = TRUE), cap), title = paste0(COLOUR_BY, "<br><small>on the walking route</small>"), opacity = 1) |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("Routes", "Output Areas", "Schools"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
```

## Height profiles

Each profile is the ground height every 50 m along the walking route.
Point *i* is *50·i* m from home, and the last point is the school, at
`route_m`. These are the `N_PROFILES` pairs in `sel` with the most
`PROFILE_ORDER`. To draw particular pairs instead, set `pick` to a few
rows of `sel`, e.g. `pick <- filter(sel, oa21cd == "E00085094")`.

```{r profiles}
#| fig-height: 6
# Height profiles for a set of pairs (needs oa21cd, urn, route_m, label) in one authority
read_profiles <- function(pairs, la, step = 50) {
  x <- open_dataset(out_dir("profiles")) |>
    filter(la == !!la, oa21cd %in% !!unique(pairs$oa21cd), urn %in% !!unique(pairs$urn)) |>   # only these Output Areas and schools
    collect() |>
    inner_join(pairs |> select(oa21cd, urn, route_m, label), by = c("oa21cd", "urn"))
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    z <- as.integer(x$elev_dm[[i]]) / 10
    d <- pmin(seq(0, by = step, length.out = length(z)), x$route_m[i]); d[length(d)] <- x$route_m[i]
    tibble(oa21cd = x$oa21cd[i], urn = x$urn[i], label = x$label[i], distance_m = d, height_m = z)
  }))
}

pick <- sel |> slice_max(.data[[PROFILE_ORDER]], n = N_PROFILES, with_ties = FALSE)
pr <- read_profiles(pick, LA)
if (PROFILE_DIRECTION == "to_home") pr <- pr |> group_by(label) |> mutate(distance_m = max(distance_m) - distance_m) |> ungroup()

ggplot(pr, aes(distance_m / 1000, height_m)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#C9B6E4", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "#4B2D7F", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_x", labeller = label_wrap_gen(40)) +
  labs(x = if (PROFILE_DIRECTION == "to_home") "Distance from school (km)" else "Distance from home (km)", y = "Ground height (m)",
       title = paste("Walking routes: height every 50 m,", sub("_", " ", PROFILE_DIRECTION))) +
  theme_minimal(11)
```

## Cycling routes, worked out on demand {#cycling-routes}

Only cycling *times* are saved nationally, so this routes the same pairs
as the height profiles (`pick`) by bike now, with the national run's
settings: 12 km/h, on quiet streets only (LTS 2) and on any street a
bike may use (LTS 4), up to 60 minutes. It uses `bike_routes()` from
`R/bike_routes.R`, which loads the street network of each pair's tile
(`data/net/<tile>`): about a minute and a few GB of memory the first
time, more for the London tiles. Set `BIKE_ROUTES <- FALSE` to skip it.
To route other pairs, pass any data frame with `oa21cd` and `urn`, e.g.
`bike_routes(filter(sel, oa21cd == "E00085094"))`.

The cycling times here should match `bike_min_lts2` and `bike_min_lts4`
to within a minute. The climb is now that of the cycle route.

```{r bike-route}
source(here::here("R", "bike_routes.R"))
bk <- if (BIKE_ROUTES) bike_routes(pick)          # NULL when BIKE_ROUTES is FALSE, and the next chunks do nothing

compare <- if (!is.null(bk)) bind_rows(
  pick |> transmute(label, oa21cd, urn, mode = "Walk", minutes = walk_min_r5, route_km = round(route_m / 1000, 2),
                    climb_to_school_m, climb_to_home_m, steep8_to_school_m),
  st_drop_geometry(bk) |> inner_join(select(pick, oa21cd, urn, label), by = c("oa21cd", "urn")) |>
    transmute(label, oa21cd, urn, mode = lts_label, minutes = bike_min_route, route_km = round(bike_route_m / 1000, 2),
              climb_to_school_m, climb_to_home_m, steep8_to_school_m)) |>
  arrange(label, mode)
compare
```

```{r bike-map}
#| fig-height: 7
modes <- c("Walk" = "#4B2D7F", "Bike, quiet streets (LTS 2)" = "#1B9E77", "Bike, any street (LTS 4)" = "#E07A1F")
if (!is.null(bk)) {
wk <- read_routes(pick, LA) |> mutate(mode = "Walk")
lines <- rbind(wk[, c("oa21cd", "urn", "mode")], mutate(bk, mode = lts_label)[, c("oa21cd", "urn", "mode")]) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  left_join(compare |> select(oa21cd, urn, mode, label, minutes, route_km, climb_to_school_m), by = c("oa21cd", "urn", "mode"))

m <- leaflet() |> addProviderTiles(BASEMAP)
for (md in names(modes)) {
  l <- filter(lines, mode == md)
  if (nrow(l)) m <- m |> addPolylines(data = l, color = modes[[md]], weight = 3, opacity = 0.8, group = md,
                                      popup = ~sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>%s: %.0f min, %.2f km, climb to school %.0f m", label, mode, minutes, route_km, climb_to_school_m),
                                      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 6, opacity = 1, bringToFront = TRUE))
}
m |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = distinct(pick, oa21cd, o_lon, o_lat), lng = ~o_lon, lat = ~o_lat, radius = 4, color = "#333333", weight = 1,
                   fillOpacity = 0.8, label = ~oa21cd) |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = distinct(pick, urn, name, s_lon, s_lat), lng = ~s_lon, lat = ~s_lat, radius = 6, color = "#222222",
                   fillColor = "white", weight = 2, fillOpacity = 1, label = ~name) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = unname(modes), labels = names(modes), opacity = 1) |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = names(modes), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}
```

Height along each route to school, walking against cycling:

```{r bike-profiles}
#| fig-height: 6
if (!is.null(bk)) {
both <- bind_rows(
  read_profiles(pick, LA) |> mutate(mode = "Walk"),
  bike_profiles(bk) |> as_tibble() |> inner_join(select(pick, oa21cd, urn, label), by = c("oa21cd", "urn")))
ggplot(both, aes(distance_m / 1000, height_m, colour = mode)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = modes, breaks = names(modes), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_x", labeller = label_wrap_gen(40)) +
  labs(x = "Distance from home (km)", y = "Ground height (m)") +
  theme_minimal(11) + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## Recipes {#recipes}

Small examples to copy, change and run. Each one uses `od`, `sel` and
the helpers above.

### One Output Area to every school it can reach

```{r recipe-one-oa}
one <- "E00085094"   # change me (it must be in LA)
od |> filter(oa21cd == one) |>
  inner_join(schools |> select(urn, name, phase), by = "urn") |>
  select(name, phase, walk_min_r5, tobler_min_to_school, climb_to_school_m, climb_to_home_m, bike_min_lts2, bike_min_lts4) |>
  arrange(walk_min_r5)
```

### Where the nearest secondary school is uphill

Each Output Area's nearest secondary school by walking time, and how far
you climb to get there. The dots are Output Area centroids, coloured by
that climb.

```{r recipe-nearest-uphill}
#| fig-height: 6
near <- od |>
  inner_join(schools |> filter(serves_secondary) |> select(urn, name), by = "urn") |>
  group_by(oa21cd) |> slice_min(walk_min_r5, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() |>
  left_join(origins |> select(oa21cd, lon, lat), by = "oa21cd")
pal2 <- colorNumeric(viridisLite::magma(256, direction = -1, end = 0.92), domain = range(near$climb_to_school_m))
leaflet(near) |> addProviderTiles(BASEMAP) |>
  addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE, fillOpacity = 0.85, fillColor = ~pal2(climb_to_school_m),
                   label = ~sprintf("%s: %s, %d min walk, %.0f m climb", oa21cd, name, walk_min_r5, climb_to_school_m)) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal2, values = ~climb_to_school_m, title = "Climb to nearest<br>secondary (m)", opacity = 1)
```

### Flat time against slope-adjusted time

How much hills add to the walk. Points above the line take longer than
on the flat.

```{r recipe-tobler}
ggplot(sel, aes(route_m / 80, tobler_min_to_school)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8, colour = "#4B2D7F") +
  geom_abline(linetype = "22") +
  labs(x = "Walking time on the flat, route length at 4.8 km/h (min)", y = "Tobler time to school (min)") +
  theme_minimal(11)
```

### Walking against cycling

```{r recipe-bike}
sel |> filter(!is.na(bike_min_lts4)) |>
  ggplot(aes(walk_min_r5, bike_min_lts4)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8, colour = "#4B2D7F") +
  geom_point(aes(y = bike_min_lts2), alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8, colour = "#E07A1F", data = ~ filter(.x, !is.na(bike_min_lts2))) +
  labs(x = "Walking time (min)", y = "Cycling time (min)", caption = "Purple: any street (LTS 4). Orange: quiet streets only (LTS 2).") +
  theme_minimal(11)
```

### Across all of England, without loading it

Arrow works on the files where they are and returns only the answer.
This counts pairs and Output Areas by authority, reading just two
columns from every file.

```{r recipe-england}
#| eval: false
od_open() |>
  filter(walk_min_r5 <= 20) |>
  group_by(la) |>
  summarise(pairs = n(), output_areas = n_distinct(oa21cd)) |>
  collect() |>
  arrange(desc(pairs))
```

### Save what you chose

```{r recipe-save}
#| eval: false
readr::write_csv(select(sel, -label), "my_pairs.csv")
st_write(st_transform(rt, 27700), "my_routes.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE)   # open in QGIS
readr::write_csv(pr, "my_profiles.csv")
```

## Things to try

- **Another place:** change `LA`, and set `ORIGINS` to a few codes from
  `oa_near()`.
- **One school's catchment on foot:** `SCHOOL_NAME <- "Stringer"`,
  `MAX_WALK_MIN <- 30`, `COLOUR_BY <- "tobler_min_to_school"`.
- **Primary schools within 15 minutes:** `PHASE <- "primary"`,
  `MAX_WALK_MIN <- 15`, `NEAREST_ONLY <- TRUE`.
- **Where quiet-street cycling is long or missing:**
  `COLOUR_BY <- "bike_min_lts2"`. Grey routes have no quiet-street route
  within 60 minutes.
- **The hilliest journeys home:** `PROFILE_ORDER <- "climb_to_home_m"`,
  `PROFILE_DIRECTION <- "to_home"`.
- **Your own filter:** after the `select` chunk, add a line such as
  `sel <- filter(sel, steep8_to_school_m > 200)`, then run the map and
  profile chunks again.
